newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - March 26.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its business page on March 26:
NEW YORK - With the Federal Reserve policymakers' decision to raise short-term interest rates, the stock market may finally enter its new era.
WASHINGTON - The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, in a remarkable turnabout, has recommended that federal auto safety officials allow consumers to deactivate air bags in their cars.
WASHINGTON - Giant Food Inc said yesterday that its fourth-quarter earnings dropped 60 percent because of the one-two punch of a five-week strike by its truck drivers and a particularly warm winter.

WASHINGTON - To hear the Clinton administration tell it, the economic benefits of U.S.-China trade were on vivid display in Beijing's Great Hall of the People on Tuesday, when Vice President Gore and Chinese Premier Li Peng toasted the signing of $2.4 billion in Chinese contracts for Boeing Co. and General Motors Corp.

WASHINGTON - In the speculative world of Internet retailing, where cold, hard sales have lagged hype and hope, bookseller Amazon.com Inc. is often cited as the shining success. Never mind that the Seattle company lost $5.8 million last year -- at least it could point to $15.7 million in revenue.
